title: Threshold and rate
summary: Past the brim, a harder pour means more tips per minute.

cards.text:
If rest sits above the brim, the water cannot stay still.
It hits the line, tips, empties, and climbs again.

cards.lead: Brim at 4. You empty on every tip.
lines: A small pour reaches the brim every 4 moments.
A harder pour reaches it every 2 moments.
More pour, more tips. That count per minute is the spike rate.

question.prompt: What does a harder pour do, once you are past the brim?
question.why: You climb back to the brim faster, so the rate goes up.
question.simpler: Rate is just how often the bucket tips.

question.prompt: A pour reaches the brim every 2 moments. In 6 moments, how many tips?
question.simpler: Divide the time by the gap between tips.

recall.question: Above threshold, what does a stronger pour do to the spike rate?

deeper.note: Threshold is the brim. Rate is how often you cross it. Abbott’s note is the historical bucket. Adrian later measured rate as impulses per second.

paper.title: Lapicque's introduction of the integrate-and-fire model neuron (1907)
paper.section: Threshold as a separate rule from the leak. Rate is the count of crossings.

terms.definition: The voltage θ the membrane must reach before the neuron emits a spike.
Spikes per unit time. Above threshold, a stronger input usually raises it.
What happens to the voltage right after a spike, so the neuron can fire again.
